target_nodes.review: The conceptual comparison now supports the question and results. The author-dependent method gaps persist. Identification of the evidence behind the reported run actions is still open.
Two plausible denominators for a daily average motivate testing the same questions under different access conditions.
The calendar-day example explains how two readings of the same records yield different answers. Related work and the chosen operational cases motivate the comparison.
The question names the two models, both context conditions, and the comparison with a reference answer for each case.
The objective asks for the share of matching answers as well as the case and repetition patterns, anticipating different denominators.
The two uses concern empirical evidence about task accuracy and an example of designing context and evaluation for similar analysis.
The claim concerns empirical accuracy on the operational cases and stays within the comparison.
The design and results may inform documentation and model decisions for similar needs. The wording promises no production benefit.
The numbered scope separates case population, synthetic data, common access, document availability and the observed output.
Fifteen cases in nine task types delimit the five operational areas.
They are synthetic rows constructed from the operational schema and business rules, distinct from the 180 returned answers.
Both use source, master and configuration data. Code, completed analyses and reference answers are withheld.
The seven documents vary together. Their individual contributions are explicitly outside scope.
Structure and values support accuracy and changes across repetitions for the fixed cases.
Five separate rows align chapter, title and function, including methods, six result groups and the final answer.
The theory chapter now moves from shared agent behavior and context to separate model characteristics and answer evaluation. The study-specific selection question is tracked in Chapter III.
The judge and the executed query output now have distinct roles in the literature summary.
The eight rows distinguish interactive tasks, open-ended insight evaluation, single-query context exposure and multistep reference-based evaluation.

The model selects a tool and its arguments, reads an observation and may request more information. A schema lookup makes the sequence concrete.
The function and argument description precede the distinction among host, client and server. The document-analysis example illustrates separate tool functions.
Monthly volume connects a request to grouping, filtering and summation. Domain meanings explain where a table name alone can leave the result ambiguous.

The first substantive reference to SKILL.md locates the routing instruction, while the cross-topic example stays in methods.
§2.7 identifies the shared ability to request data and the two availability conditions. Its last sentence qualifies the informational value of the equal nominal windows.
§2.7.1 attributes multistep behavior to Meta and illustrates a possible schema-to-data request. Table 2.2 retains the numerical capacity and sources.
§2.7.2 identifies the served version and connects its documented tool and JSON capabilities to the two parts of the task. The text locates the JSON requirement in the prompt.
Reference-based evaluation fits definite answers. The next three sections distinguish a decision on one object, a proportion across objects, and three outcomes on one fixed case.
Required attributes, types, array order and values all contribute to a single all-or-nothing verdict. Methods specify numeric and object-order exceptions.
The numerator counts matching answers and all three repetitions enter the relevant condition. The methods formula and grouping clarify the denominator.
The case, model and condition are held fixed over three runs. Zero and three successes distinguish consistently unsuccessful and consistently successful outcomes.
The opening places preparation before generation and assessment. The registered details let readers compute run counts and reconstruct a worked score.
The evaluator uses inaccessible reference answers. Both models share prompts, data, tools and cases while access to business documents varies.
The numbering example and four rows give 15 cases × 3 runs = 45 answers in each cell, with 90 per model.
The heading introduces both operational data read by the agent and separately constructed reference answers used in scoring.
The methods distinguish 237 rows across 15 operational tables from master and configuration data. The prompt limits the requested subset despite wider read access.
Case selection connects available business analyses to distinct reasoning demands, including cross-table relationships and period or threshold conditions.
The examples distinguish non-null weighted pooling, missing days, all-action completion, repeated causes, scope exceptions, and status comparisons.
One row per case connects challenge to capability. The worsened status reported for T9-C2 needs per-indicator outcomes to reconcile with the later illustration.
The reference is computed from the appropriate data, encoded as JSON and kept fixed for all runs. The following rules and calculation give the procedure substance.
Table 3.4 specifies inclusive dates, monthly zero-volume classes, eligible accidents and repeated assignments, non-null observations, and threshold comparison before rounding.
Six booth observations and one longbooth observation are in scope. The table separates their counts and totals before the equations.
The six ten-second observations and one two-second observation sum to 62 seconds.
All seven observations are non-null. Dividing 62 by 7 gives 8.86 seconds in the named output attribute, distinct from other fields of its object.
The unchanged system prompt is displayed and the text differentiates it from the per-case request and separately accessible documents.
The request names the task and schema. Data names, formulas and solution steps are withheld; schema, ordering and rounding constrain representation.
The T2-C1 example specifies period, integer rounding and vehicle-class order but leaves the calendar-day denominator to the analysis.
Development knowledge supplied the rule content. A routing file and six domain references define the intervention package; the enabling procedure remains unspecified.
The map names the routing document and six references, tying each to data selection, computation or status interpretation.
The quoted instruction and the transaction-plus-indicator example explain how to find two references when a question spans topics.
This organizing heading introduces model settings, data access and independent conversations in the necessary order.
The shared runtime, version, reasoning labels, context and distinct output limits are reported. The text describes provider sampling defaults and gives numbers without explaining model choice.
Entity discovery, schema inspection and paginated record reads explain the available data path. The conditional skill documents are a separate input.
Three new conversations with identical case prompts and fixed reference answers explain the repeated unit. The description does not say what intermediate evidence was retained.
The introduction states the per-answer decision. The following sequence establishes a judgment rule, a denominator, and separate pooled and crossed analyses.
JSON validity, structural and numeric equality, array ordering, and irrelevant property order define the decision. The actual evaluator or checking procedure is unnamed.
The expected and matching objects agree. An additional cause and an excessive count change two details and the total from five to seven in the failed object.
The displayed ratio uses all judged answers in the subset shown, including all three repetitions. Forty-five per model-condition and zero to three per fixed case have different interpretations.
For two cases the two marginal comparisons each pool 12 answers, while each configuration contains six. Six task groups and case-level repeat counts are specified.

The distribution reconciles 237 input rows with 15 cases, four conditions and 180 replies. Each group’s answer count follows from its case count.
The parent groups both duration cases and introduces marginal and joint comparisons.
Both pooled conditions achieve 12/12. The discussion checks variable record counts and the two record sources entering the means.
Both models achieve 12/12. The two correct means, 23.09 and 8.86 seconds, identify what was compared.
All four cells have 6/6 from two cases, and each case has 3/3 within each cell.
The traffic group separates weekly and monthly tasks before presenting model and context comparisons.
Scores are 12/12 versus 8/12. All four failures involve incomplete class details on the monthly case.
Eleven versus nine successes out of twelve reflect incomplete monthly class coverage when documents were unavailable.
The four configuration counts isolate T3-C1. The weekly case passes throughout.
The missing zero-volume class for January and February accounts for the failures even though the returned values match. Claims about the chosen source need run evidence.
The group first distinguishes status from accident-cause frequencies, then compares conditions and models.
The eligible-incident status counts match in every run. Both failures concern cause distribution.
Results of 10/12 and 12/12 locate both failures in the first model without documents.
The affected model drops from 6/6 to 4/6; the two failures are the first and third runs of T5-C1.
The expected and observed totals are five and seven. One added category and one inflated frequency match the extra two assignments; specific reading actions need provenance.
The group reports one case using the two marginal and one joint comparison.
All six answers in each context match. Four damaged items include an item without priority, so P1/P2 counts sum to three.
Both models score 6/6. Three damaged items are assigned to the shoulder and one to lane 1 in the reference.
Each model-condition achieves 3/3 on the single inspection case.
The group covers four report-level cases before breaking out the four discrepant answers.
Twenty-four versus twenty of 24 answers pass. Three failures have incorrect statuses and one lacks required evaluations.
Twenty-three versus twenty-one of 24 pass. All between-model differences arise without documents.
The models obtain 11/12 and 9/12 without documents. Two cases always pass and the remaining two supply the four failures.
The table distinguishes three status errors from the partial four-of-twenty answer and links them to specific runs.
The raw 6.004 and 9.004 values exceed the respective thresholds. Displayed rounded values can equal them. The returned status and claimed order of an agent’s calculations require different evidence.
The reference needs 20 evaluations across four booths and five indicators. The answer omits 16. Reading configuration and choosing only one indicator are claims about actions.
Four cases test status over a period or a change between periods. All four cells are reported.
Both pooled conditions reach 24/24. The measured outputs include within-period statuses and cross-period changes.
Both reach 24/24 with counts and status matching. A nonapplicable service requirement is represented separately from a failed one.
Each of four configurations achieves 12/12, with 3/3 in each of four cases.
Four failures rise to eight of eight on indicator four, yet it fails in both periods. The row describing a worsened status may refer to another indicator.
Edited repeat account introduces the case consistently failing before giving the alternating cases. The treatment and utility limitations still bound the conclusions.
Both models reach 45/45 with documents, versus 41/45 and 39/45 without. The affected groups differ by model.
Omitted elements, extra assignments and incorrect booleans correspond to concrete output discrepancies. Direct assertions about how an agent calculated need independent support.
